meta.title: Devotion Race Atlas
meta.intro: Each race's devotion architecture from high altitude: the progression spine, the culture substrate, the curse layer, and the Daedric track - every node marked by how real it is today. Design intent from the race sheets; build status from live-source with file evidence.
meta.statusLine: Papyrus/static atlas reconciled against the active Devotion Dev load order and Devotion.esp record/VMAD readback on 2026-08-24. Runtime and player-surface proof remain separate.
meta.owner: This JSON is the AUTHORITY. The HTML is generated by tools/pdv_atlas_render.mjs and is NOT committed. Edit nodes here; regenerate to view.

legend.label: Built - verified in live source, evidence cited
Partial - built, with a verified defect or gap
Designed only - in the design docs, absent from source
Absent - nothing found in design or source

readingGuide: Four lanes per race, left to right in time. Spine is the progression walk. Substrate is the always-on culture layer (three races run it inline without a metric). Curse shows how vampirism and lycanthropy land for that race. The Daedric progression is identical for all ten races, so it is drawn once below; each race page carries only its Daedric flavor.
notes: Vocabulary. Chips carry the real moment IDs (tier.reach, focus.emergence, dawn.digest...). Piety thresholds: Seeker 25 - Devoted 50 - Champion 85. Substrate metric 0-75, tiers at 1/25/75, one shared 4.0/day credit budget.

Two findings that frame every page. The Marked surfacing rung (arch 10.6: "moments the player should remember") has no implementation for any race - all contextual favor exits one generic toast call. And the coverage map's rule that the Devoted crossing surfaces via emergence is design intent only: Khajiit is the sole race with a real emergence beat; the only other emergence.onset emitter (Breton) is provably unreachable, and every other race rides the generic tier lane.

matrix.note: What the matrix says. The spine and substrates are solidly built everywhere they're meant to exist. The unevenness is concentrated in the announcement layer: champion entry is a Kyne-only feature shown through the standard path, emergence is Khajiit-only, and five races handle curses correctly while telling the player nothing. Two dead state keys (Orc and Redguard VampireScar) and the Dunmer no-decay question are the loose bolts. This matches the tranche's running theme: the mod computes state transitions reliably and announces them inconsistently.

queue.question: Should the Marked surfacing rung be built as a real capability, or should the 19 historical Marked-tier beats be deliberately retired?
queue.papyrusResult: Architecture v3 section 10.6 defines a three-rung ladder Quiet/Noted/Marked, Marked being a named notification or message reserved for moments the player should remember, and permits costly-but-faithful events to surface one level above their duration bucket. Quiet and Noted are live. Marked has NO implementation for any race: no identifier matching FavorMarked/_Marked/MarkedSurfac exists in live-source/Scripts/Source; PDV_ContextualFavorRuntime.psc models no surfacing-level constant (MARKED and QUIET appear only inside favor FAMILY names such as FAVOR_FAMILY_KYNE_WIND_MARKED_PASSAGE); and every contextual favor exits through one call at PDV_ContextualFavorRuntime.psc:177 -- SendPrismaEventToast('favor', favorDeity, contextText, '', ''). A cheap favor and a costly one are surfaced identically. Route claims are repo-mirror-derived and remain version-qualified until shared.runtime-wiring.version-drift is resolved.
queue.espResult: 19 historical FavorMarked rows exist in the disposition audit; 4 are classified 'Reconcile to current runtime' against records that are demonstrably different moments (Imperial Talos defiance mapped to a Hermaeus Mora scholarship response; Breton irreversible rupture mapped to the origin-choice confirm prompt; Redguard hard passage mapped to Ash'abah entry/survey lines), so that bucket is over-counted for this tier. ESP readback NOT performed -- Papyrus-source verified only; direct houseCARL readback owed, Codex-owned.
queue.implementationRoute: New event name on the already-wired typed payload: SendPrismaEventToast(eventName, deity, context, tierLabel, rival, allowFallback) builds JSON keyed on the event and already degrades via BuildPrismaEventFallbackText to a vanilla notification. Pair with a Book of Days entry for permanence. Constraints: the Prisma index.html cache key must be bumped or the view change never reaches the running game; the heading must resolve GetPublicDeityDisplayName rather than the symbol; diegetic channels are D0-gated and the fallback loses the title; the one-per-event cooldown belongs on the pulse, not only on the presentation.
queue.runtimeProof: Required: new event dispatched from the high-cost branch; toast seen in game with the public deity name; the same beat with the Prisma bridge down; per-event cooldown observed across repeated qualifying acts; one-shot state surviving reload.

queue.question: How should the Sithis activation crossing be distinguished from the post-activation signals that currently reuse its wording?
queue.papyrusResult: THREE distinct defects, not one. (i) The crossing is never detected as an event: VoidActivationSignalsRequired = 3 at PDV_Substrate_ArgonianHist.psc:25; IsVoidFullyActive() at :352-354 gates on a SithisSignalCount accumulator; RecordVoidSignalScaled at :115-128 increments with AdjustIntValue(...,1) at :124 and never reads the prior value. The only other writes are a debug setter (PDV_DebugRuntime.psc:206) and a reset to zero (:392). (ii) The threshold phrase never stops firing: HandleArgonianVoidSignal (PDV_OriginRuntime_Argonian.psc:829-843) awards only when already active (:841), and that award routes AwardCuratedSignalScaled to AwardPiety(..., CuratedSignalDriverReason(...)) to AwardPietyInternal, which calls RecordDeityDriver and SendPrismaEventToast.
